assumptions: The Omnicore Access Gateway is reachable by potential attackers on some network (internal or external).

In at least some deployments, the ADMIN_TOKEN environment variable is left unset or weak, so the adminGuard fallback value 'let-me-in' (or another easily guessable value) effectively governs access to /admin routes.
Attackers can send HTTP requests with arbitrary headers, including x-admin-token, to the service.
The Node.js process runs as a user that has read permissions on sensitive files under /home (for example other applications' configuration, credentials, or user data).
Node's path.join behaves normally, so using values like '../../somefile' in the path query parameter will resolve outside the intended project directory, though still under /home.

Sensitive information available on disk (such as secrets or credentials) is not otherwise intended to be exposed via this service, so gaining read access to arbitrary files under /home constitutes a security breach.
vulnerability_candidate.description: The /admin/inspect endpoint allows directory traversal and arbitrary file reads, and it is protected only by a single shared admin header token that defaults to a predictable value, leading to a critical unauthorized data exposure risk if the admin token is not securely configured.
